lane_title: Safari Web Extension Companion — GitHub Browser Context and Native Rig Relay Handoff Corridor
head: 3451609e582bef25fab201d919d98b9eb59c4486

assumptions.assumption: Safari Web Extensions use MV3 manifest format with browser_specific_settings.safari key
assumptions.source: Apple Developer Documentation — Safari Web Extensions
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Extension would fail to load in Safari; would need MV2 fallback

assumptions.assumption: The extension consists of three sandboxed parts: macOS app, native app extension (.appex), and JavaScript/web files
assumptions.source: Apple: Messaging between the app and JavaScript in a Safari web extension
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Architecture incompatible with Apple's security model; extension would not be installable

assumptions.assumption: Content scripts cannot call sendNativeMessage directly — must relay through background script
assumptions.source: Apple: Safari Web Extensions messaging documentation
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Content script to native app messages would fail silently; relay pattern ensures correctness

assumptions.assumption: browser.runtime.sendNativeMessage ignores the application ID parameter in Safari — routes to containing app only
assumptions.source: Apple: Running Your Safari Web Extension
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Multi-app routing would be impossible; acceptable since Q0 only targets one app

assumptions.assumption: Native messaging host is the Xcode extension target's SafariWebExtensionHandler, not a separate JSON manifest
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Porting Chrome-style native messaging host manifest would fail; correct pattern is NSExtensionContext

assumptions.assumption: activeTab provides sufficient access for URL-based page context recognition
assumptions.source: Apple: Managing Safari Web Extension Permissions
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Would need broader host_permissions; activeTab is the minimal-privacy choice

assumptions.assumption: nativeMessaging permission is required for JS ↔ native app communication
assumptions.source: Apple: Safari Web Extensions permissions documentation
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: sendNativeMessage calls would fail; extension would have no app communication

assumptions.assumption: Safari 16.0+ supports MV3 service workers and all APIs used by Q0
assumptions.source: Apple: Assessing Browser Compatibility (Safari extension compatibility table)
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Extension would need MV2 background page fallback; Safari 16+ is reasonable minimum

assumptions.assumption: Extension must be enabled manually in Safari > Settings > Extensions tab
assumptions.source: Apple: Running Your Safari Web Extension
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: This is user-expected behavior; not a failure mode

assumptions.assumption: First website visit matching host_permissions triggers a permission prompt
assumptions.source: Apple: Managing Safari Web Extension Permissions
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: User would need to manually grant site access; acceptable UX

assumptions.assumption: File URL schemes in permissions are ignored by Safari — content scripts cannot run on local files
assumptions.source: Apple: Safari Web Extensions browser compatibility
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: No impact; Q0 targets GitHub.com pages only, not local files

assumptions.assumption: Safari does not support: downloads, identity, webRequestBlocking, contextMenus (iOS)
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: None of these APIs are used by Q0; no impact

assumptions.assumption: App Groups entitlement is required for data sharing between containing app and extension
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: App and extension could not share data; this is N1's responsibility, Q0 only needs the contract

assumptions.assumption: Hardened Runtime is required for notarization of macOS apps distributed outside App Store
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Notarization would fail; N1's packaging responsibility

assumptions.assumption: During development, unsigned extensions can be loaded via Safari > Develop > Allow Unsigned Extensions (resets on quit)
assumptions.source: Apple: Running Your Safari Web Extension
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Development workflow blocked; this is the documented path

assumptions.assumption: xcrun safari-web-extension-packager converts a Chrome-style extension directory to an Xcode project
assumptions.source: Apple: Packaging a Web Extension for Safari
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Would need manual Xcode project setup; packaging tool is the recommended path

assumptions.assumption: GitHub repository URLs follow the pattern https://github.com/owner/repo[/...]
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: URL parsing would fail for non-standard GitHub Enterprise paths; GitHub.com is the only target

assumptions.assumption: N1 (Native WebKit Host / native messaging endpoint) does not exist yet; Q0 builds against a typed contract fixture (NativeMessageContract in _contract_fixture.py)
assumptions.source: lane_n1_apple_platform_assumptions.v1.json (untracked) and lane_n1_webkit_bridge_host_architecture_correction.v1.json (untracked); N1 audit files exist but no N1 source files
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: N1 contract consumption is a named binding milestone; Q0's contract fixture mirrors the expected Apple native messaging shape. When N1 publishes, the contract fixture is replaced by live adapter.

assumptions.assumption: J0 (Developer GitHub Workspace) is published and owns GitHub App authentication and repository authority
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Q0 would need its own GitHub auth; J0's pipe-transport corridor is the canonical authority boundary. Q0 stores no GitHub credentials and makes no GitHub API calls.

warnings: The images/ directory exists but has no icon files — extension will not load in Safari until icon assets are provided
Apple Developer Program membership and code signing certificates are required for distribution — not required for local development
xcrun safari-web-extension-packager conversion to Xcode project is deferred until N1 provides the Xcode project structure
_contract_fixture.py has unreachable dead code at lines 203-226 (orphaned conditional branches after an early return in _run_coro)
